episode.subject: common milkweed
episode.title: The next mouth
episode.body:
One of the aphids had a daughter without leaving my stem. The daughter put her mouth down beside her mother's.

I kept sending sap toward the new leaves.

It was becoming difficult to tell whose family I was raising.

proposals.visualReview: Opened original and exact published display individually. No birth itself is visible. No taxon is asserted for the aphids and no brown body is interpreted as a predator.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Birth and mother-daughter relationship are remembered fictional context compatible with aphid summer viviparity, not a photographed event. No deliberate sap control, poison resistance, infestation lethality or measured growth rate is claimed.
proposals.canon: Established Asclepias syriaca perennial, Minnesota meadow home unchanged. Seasonal recollection before seed maturation; no reversal of opened pods. Her wish to direct generosity becomes uncertainty about which family her sap supports. Distinct from held pod/welcome-mat defense joke; possible conceptual overlap with admitted caterpillar consumption remains for lead judgment. No new identity/avatar.
